answer: Agents bond stake before joining an epoch and derive rate-limit shares from an epoch polynomial committed in the identity tree. Semaphore proofs bind each message to a nullifier without exposing the agent’s identity. Reusing that nullifier produces distinct Shamir shares; anyone can interpolate them to recover the signing secret and submit evidence for immediate collateral slashing. A willow- and sable-labeled epoch may use a cipher-based commitment, but secrecy does not excuse duplicate messages.
